title: perf(canary): adaptive thresholds + hysteresis for automated detection and rollout guards
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add adaptive thresholding and hysteresis to performance canary detector; improves sensitivity per-route/model and reduces flapping during traffic variance. Backwards-compatible config flags expose tuning knobs for rollout guards.
description: Context: our production canary service (perf-canary) has been using static thresholds for latency and throughput regressions which leads to either noisy false positives during traffic shifts or missed slow drifts when thresholds are too loose. This PR implements adaptive thresholds and a hysteresis layer to make automated detection more robust and to reduce canary-induced rollbacks. Motivation: reduce noisy rollbacks, catch gradual regressions, and allow per-route/model sensitivity tuning without manual threshold hunting. Design summary: 1) per-route rolling baseline that computes median and P95 distributions over multiple window sizes (1m, 5m, 1h) and maintains an exponential decay to weight recent traffic; 2) adaptive threshold calculation that combines baseline variance, model-specific multipliers, and historical anomaly frequency to set dynamic alert thresholds; 3) hysteresis state machine that requires sustained anomaly score above threshold for a configurable duration before marking a canary failing, and similarly requires sustained recovery before promoting; 4) new rollout guard policy integration: canary manager now queries the detector for a graded anomaly score (0..100) instead of a binary flag and applies policy rules (soft-fail vs hard-fail) with automatic rollback windows; 5) config surface: schema changes in perf-canary config and a small Redwood Console UI panel to tune sensitivity, hysteresis windows, and adaptive multipliers per route/model. Implementation notes: added adaptive_thresholds.py (core algorithm), hysteresis.py (state machine and transition tests), detector adapter changes to emit anomaly_score and baseline metadata, metrics exported (canary.anomaly_score, canary.hysteresis_state, canary.threshold_value) and new dashboards in Grafana. Database: added lightweight time-series summary tables to store rolling percentiles with TTL to reduce memory pressure. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves previous static-threshold logic unless adaptive_enabled=true in config; rollout guard remains pluggable. Tests: unit tests for algorithmic correctness, integration tests that replay recorded traffic traces (including step increases and slow drifts), and e2e canary runs in perf-canary lab. CI: added a perf unit that runs a short synthetic workload to validate anomaly scoring determinism. Rollout plan: feature-gate behind config and a staged rollout (10% of internal canaries -> 50% -> 100%) with automated regression rollback if anomaly false-positive rate > 3% in pilot. Risk and mitigation: new sensitivity must be tuned; we provide sensible defaults and telemetry to iterate; hysteresis prevents immediate flapping; metric retention TTL limits storage cost. Checklist: - [x] implement adaptive threshold algorithm - [x] hysteresis state machine - [x] telemetry + dashboards - [x] config schema updates + Console UI - [x] unit & integration tests - [x] canary lab validation - [x] rollout plan and Linear link (ENG-1023).
